newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian castor ends down on higher supply.
newsitem.headline: Indian castor ends down on higher supply.

text.p: Indian castorseed September delivery ended down on improved supply and heavy speculative selling, traders said.
They said prices fell to 1,147/1,148 rupees per quintal from 1,169/1,170 rupees.
"Increased arrivals at the producing centres prompted substantial liquidation by bulls ahead of delivery while overseas buyers kept to the sidelines," a trader said.
Traders said there were no trades in December deliveries.
The daily average arrivals of castorseed in the Gujarat region rose to 13,000/14,000 bags (75 kg each), they said.
Groundnut oil fell to 365/366 rupees per 10 kg from 372 rupees on higher arrivals of 80/100 tonnes and lower than expected seasonal demand.
In Rajkot spot groundnut oil rose from 578 rupees to 584/585 rupees per 15 kg.
"Bombay market is receiving higher arrivals from southern India while inflows from the Gujarat region remained low," one miller said.
Imported palm oil fell three to four rupees to 255/256 rupees per 10 kg on increased arrivals at the Bombay port and a weak global trend.
Traders said they expected more arrivals at Bombay port in the near future and sentiment was subdued.
